facts: Roys Peak stands at an elevation of 1,578 meters above sea level near Wanaka, New Zealand.
The famous track winds through classic tussock grasslands, offering panoramic views of Lake Wanaka and Mount Aspiring.
The full day-hike covers approximately sixteen kilometers round trip with a steep, continuous uphill incline.
Lake Wanaka below Roys Peak was carved out by massive glaciers over ten thousand years ago.
The breathtaking backdrop of Mount Aspiring National Park featured prominently in Lord of the Rings films.
The iconic viewpoint along the ridge is famous worldwide for its dramatic mountain ridgeline photo spot.
Skylarks and New Zealand falcons can often be spotted soaring above the high tussock pastures.
Indigenous Maori people traditionally traveled through this region to gather food and prized greenstone.
The nearby town of Wanaka sits on the southern end of Lake Wanaka in Otago.
Wanaka is a major hub for adventure sports including trail running, skydiving, skiing, and mountain biking.
The track passes through active sheep farming land, so dogs are prohibited to protect livestock.
Nearby Mount Aspiring, or Tititea in Maori, is the highest peak outside the Mount Cook region.
The Otago region is internationally famous for producing world-class Pinot Noir wines.
Snow often covers the upper sections of the track during the Southern Hemisphere winter months.
Challenge Wanaka, held nearby every year, is considered one of the world's most scenic triathlon courses.
Tussock grass covers the slopes, helping prevent soil erosion in high alpine environments.
World champion multisport athletes train regularly in the tough alpine terrain surrounding Wanaka.
Roys Peak was named after John Roy, an early settler and surveyor in the Otago district.
Local cafes in Wanaka serve traditional Kiwi meat pies, perfect fuel for hungry runners after a climb.
Lake Wanaka reaches depths of more than three hundred meters in its deepest glacial basins.
